finding.claim: Blind SSRF via stored webhook callback URL. POST /subscribe stores an arbitrary callbackUrl with no validation (no scheme allowlist, no host/IP check, no private/loopback/metadata block). The scheduled job then POSTs the payload to every stored URL, so any caller who can subscribe can make the server send requests to internal hosts (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, localhost, internal services). The response is discarded, so the SSRF is blind, but it still allows internal POSTs and port scanning. DNS rebinding is also possible because there is no IP pinning.

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-controlled URL
URL stored unvalidated in the subscriptions map
notifyAll iterates over the stored URLs on the per-minute job
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI with no validation
client.send issues the POST from the server network position

finding.guards_checked: No auth is visible on the subscribe route (the handler is only a comment). No scheme, host or IP validation exists. No private-range blocking and no DNS pinning. The HttpClient does not follow redirects by default, but that does not mitigate the direct request to an internal target. The response body is not returned to the attacker, so impact is limited to blind SSRF.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:21-24 POSTs to it via URI.create/client.send with no scheme or host checks. The only validation in the file, the regex at line 30, applies to thumb() and not to this path.
